title: Get started with pipeflow
text: example, ’ll use base R’s airquality dataset. goal create analysis pipeline performs following steps: add new data column Temp.Celsius containing temperature degrees Celsius fit linear model data plot data model fit. following, ’ll show define run pipeline, inspect output specific steps, finally re-run pipeline different parameter settings, one selling points using pipeline.

title: Get started with pipeflow
text: easier understanding, go step step. First, create new pipeline name “-pipeline” add data step provides input dataset. step, minimum specify name step (step = "data) function (fun) defines computed step. Let’s take first look pipeline. step represented one row table, currently shows four columns: step name step params names function parameters depends dependencies step () state state step, initially always set new Next, want add step called prep, prepares original data adding new column "Temp.Celsius". means, prep step use output data step. refer output earlier pipeline step, just write name preceded tilde (~) operator, case means ~data. Since pip_add works “reference”, can add step follows: reiterate: function(df = ~data) basically means function gets called df contain whatever produced last data step. , second step called prep added depends data step, also marked 2nd row column depends. Next, want add step called fit fits linear model data. function using prepared data defines parameter xVar, determines variable used predictor linear model. Lastly, add step called plot, plots data linear model fit. function references fit prep step. previous step, defines xVar parameter plus two plot-specific parameters xLab title. depends column row 4:, see plot step depends fit prep step. addition tabular output, {pipeflow} also provides graphical representation compatible visNetwork package. pip_graph() function returns list arguments can feed directly visNetwork::visNetwork(). , pipeline visualized directed acyclic graph (DAG) nodes represent steps edges represent dependencies.
code: library(pipeflow)  pip <- pip_new("my-pip")  pip <- pip_add(     pip,     step = "data",     fun = function(data = airquality) data ) pip # <pipeflow> my-pip (1 step) # -------------------------- #    step params depends state # 1: data   data           new # -------------------------- # <ready> last run: never pip |> pip_add(     "prep",     function(df = ~data) {         df[, "Temp.Celsius"] <- (df[, "Temp"] - 32) * 5 / 9         df     } ) pip # <pipeflow> my-pip (2 steps) # --------------------------- #    step params depends state # 1: data   data           new # 2: prep     df    data   new # --------------------------- # <ready> last run: never pip |> pip_add(     "fit",     function(data = ~prep,              xVar = "Temp.Celsius") {         lm(paste("Ozone ~", xVar), data = data)     } )  pip # <pipeflow> my-pip (3 steps) # --------------------------- #    step    params depends state # 1: data      data           new # 2: prep        df    data   new # 3:  fit data,xVar    prep   new # --------------------------- # <ready> last run: never pip |> pip_add(     "plot",     function(model = ~fit,              data = ~prep,              xVar = "Temp.Celsius",              xLab = "Temperature in degrees Celsius",              title = "Linear model fit") {         require(ggplot2, quietly = TRUE)         coeffs <- coefficients(model)         ggplot(data) +             geom_point(aes(.data[[xVar]], .data[["Ozone"]])) +             geom_abline(intercept = coeffs[1], slope = coeffs[2]) +             labs(title = title, x = xLab)     } ) pip # <pipeflow> my-pip (4 steps) # --------------------------- #    step                     params  depends state # 1: data                       data            new # 2: prep                         df     data   new # 3:  fit                  data,xVar     prep   new # 4: plot model,data,xVar,xLab,title fit,prep   new # --------------------------- # <ready> last run: never library(visNetwork) do.call(visNetwork, args = pip_graph(pip)) |>     visHierarchicalLayout(direction = "LR")

title: Get started with pipeflow
text: Even moderately complex analysis consisting , say, 15 20 different functions, keeping track different analysis parameters can quickly get hand. see, {pipeflow} becomes much easier, since pipeline keeps track parameters values. Let’s first inspect parameters defined pipeline using pip_get_params() function. returns list unbound parameters (data, xVar, xLab, title). unbound mean values parameters don’t depend steps (.e. parameters defined ~ operator) therefore can adjusted freely. Also note parameter listed , even ’s used multiple steps2. change parameters, simply call pip_set_params(): {pipeflow} automatically propagates new parameter values steps use . addition, recognize steps affected parameter change mark outdated (see column state). can see fit plot steps now state outdated, xVar xLab parameters updated. update results, just run pipeline . closer look run log shows pipeline skipped first two steps ran steps outdated, basically can thought caching mimicking behavior make software development. , {pipeflow} always keeps track step states re-runs necessary. can huge time saver larger pipelines3. re-run, can see output updated accordingly now showing new x-variable Solar.R.  Let’s visit examples parameter changes effects pipeline. just change title plot, plot step needs rerun.  change input data parameter data step, since steps depend , expect steps rerun.  Last least let’s try set parameters don’t exist pipeline, mostly happens due accidental misspells. see, warning given user hinting respective parameter names, makes fixing misspells straight-forward. Next, let’s see modify pipeline.

text: Let’s say want insert new step prep step standardizes y-variable. , use pip_add() argument. standardize step now part pipeline, far used step.
code: pip |> pip_add(     "standardize",     function(data = ~prep,              yVar = "Ozone") {         data[, yVar] <- scale(data[, yVar])         data     },     after = "prep" ) pip # <pipeflow> my-pip (5 steps) # --------------------------- #           step                     params  depends state                out # 1:        data                       data           done <data.frame[10x6]> # 2:        prep                         df     data  done <data.frame[10x7]> # 3: standardize                  data,yVar     prep   new             [NULL] # 4:         fit                  data,xVar     prep  done           <lm[13]> # 5:        plot model,data,xVar,xLab,title fit,prep  done  <ggplot2::ggplot> # --------------------------- # <ready> last run: 2026-09-27 17:19:49 library(visNetwork) do.call(visNetwork, args = pip_graph(pip)) |>     visHierarchicalLayout(direction = "LR", sortMethod = "directed")

text: Let’s see pipeline . trying remove step, {pipeflow} default checks step used step, raises error removing step violate integrity pipeline enforce removing step together downstream dependencies, can use force argument. Naturally, last step never downstream dependencies, can removed without issues. Replacing steps pipeline shown vignette allow re-use existing pipelines adapt programmatically new requirements. title: Combine pipelines
text: Let’s define one pipeline used data preprocessing one modelling2.
code: library(pipeflow)  pip1 <- pip_new("preprocess") |>     pip_add("data", \(x = 1:5) x) |>     pip_add("prep", \(x = ~data) x + 1) |>     pip_add("standardize", \(x = ~prep, scale = 2) x * scale) pip2 <- pip_new("model") |>     pip_add("data", \(x = 1:5) x) |>     pip_add("fit", \(x = ~data, k = 2, b = 0) x * k + b) |>     pip_add("predict", \(x = ~fit) paste0("pred: ", x))

title: Combine pipelines
text: Next combine two pipelines using rbind(). Note data step second pipeline renamed data2 step depends columns (see line 4 ). , “rbinding” pipelines, {pipeflow} automatically ensures step names stay unique renaming duplicates accordingly. also visible graphical representation pipeline, two pipelines yet connected. make sense combined pipeline, want use output standardize step input data2 step, can applying replace function, introduced previous vignette modify pipeline, follows: data2 step points output standardize step, pipelines now connected.
code: pip <- rbind(pip1, pip2)  pip # <pipeflow> preprocess-model (6 steps) # ------------------------------------- #           step  params depends state # 1:        data       x           new # 2:        prep       x    data   new # 3: standardize x,scale    prep   new # 4:       data2       x           new # 5:         fit   x,k,b   data2   new # 6:     predict       x     fit   new # ------------------------------------- # <ready> last run: never library(visNetwork) do.call(visNetwork, args = pip_graph(pip)) |>     visHierarchicalLayout(direction = "LR") pip |> pip_replace("data2", \(x = ~standardize) x)  pip # <pipeflow> preprocess-model (6 steps) # ------------------------------------- #           step  params     depends    state # 1:        data       x                  new # 2:        prep       x        data      new # 3: standardize x,scale        prep      new # 4:       data2       x standardize      new # 5:         fit   x,k,b       data2 outdated # 6:     predict       x         fit outdated # ------------------------------------- # <ready> last run: never

title: Combine pipelines
text: Since name re-routed step might always known3, {pipeflow} package also provides relative position indexing mechanism, allows rewrite command using number (instead step name standardize) effect . relative indexing mechanism allows refer steps positioned current step. index ~-1 can interpreted “go one step back”, ~-2 “go two steps back”, .
code: pip |> pip_replace("data2", \(x = ~ -1) x)  pip # <pipeflow> preprocess-model (6 steps) # ------------------------------------- #           step  params     depends    state # 1:        data       x                  new # 2:        prep       x        data      new # 3: standardize x,scale        prep      new # 4:       data2       x standardize      new # 5:         fit   x,k,b       data2 outdated # 6:     predict       x         fit outdated # ------------------------------------- # <ready> last run: never

title: Pipeline views
text: , use simplified example pipeline. see , besides step fun, pip_add() also allows set tags. use tags meta information filter certain steps topic /output type. Let’s first run move .
code: library(pipeflow)  pip <- pip_new("my-pip") |>     pip_add("load", \(n = 5) seq_len(n), tags = c("io", "daily")) |>     pip_add("clean", \(x = ~load) x * 2, tags = c("io", "core")) |>     pip_add("fit", \(x = ~clean) sum(x), tags = c("model", "core")) |>     pip_add("report", \(x = ~fit) paste("result:", x), tags = "report") (pip_run(pip, lgr = NULL)) # <pipeflow> my-pip (4 steps) # --------------------------- #      step params depends state            out       tags # 1:   load      n          done      1,2,3,4,5   io,daily # 2:  clean      x    load  done  2, 4, 6, 8,10    io,core # 3:    fit      x   clean  done             30 model,core # 4: report      x     fit  done     result: 30     report # --------------------------- # <ready> last run: 2026-09-27 17:19:55

title: Pipeline views

title: Pipeline views

title: Nested pipelines
text: outer pipeline splits data subsets derives model coefficients running inner pipeline split. Note inner_run step: parameters xVar yVar forwarded inner pipeline.
code: # Helper to run inner pipeline run_inner_pip <- function(pip, name, data) {     pip$name <- sprintf("coefs for *%s*", name)      # Set data subset for inner pipeline and run it     pip_set_params(pip, list(data = data)) |> pip_run()      pip[["coefs", "out"]] }  outer <- pip_new("full analysis") |>     pip_add("data", \(data = NULL) data) |>     pip_add(         "split_data", \(data = ~data, byVar = "by") {             split(data, f = data[[byVar]])         }     ) |>     pip_add(         "inner_run",         \(dataList = ~split_data, xVar = "x", yVar = "y") {             p <- pip_clone(inner)              # Forward parameters to inner             pip_set_params(p, list(xVar = xVar, yVar = yVar))              Map(                 f = run_inner_pip,                 name = names(dataList),                 data = dataList,                 MoreArgs = list(pip = p)             )         }     ) |>     pip_add(         "combine",         \(coefs = ~inner_run) as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, coefs))     )  outer # <pipeflow> full analysis (4 steps) # ---------------------------------- #          step             params    depends state # 1:       data               data              new # 2: split_data         data,byVar       data   new # 3:  inner_run dataList,xVar,yVar split_data   new # 4:    combine              coefs  inner_run   new # ---------------------------------- # <ready> last run: never

title: Nested pipelines
text: forwarding parameters manually inner pipeline straight-forward toy example, trying manually synchronize real-world parameter sets outer inner pipeline quickly becomes unfeasible source bugs hard detect. reason, practice, following pattern used, basically just forwards combined set existing parameters. , replace inner_run step follows: version, inner_run step longer declares xVar yVar arguments. what: Built-in exec modes vs. nested pipelines
title: Nested pipelines
text: previous vignette solve “split, apply, combine” problem. built-execution modes (exec = "split"/"reduce") recommended default whenever fit nested pipelines can considered general tool. rule thumb: Code: built-modes declarative need extra code, nested pattern requires cloning, mapping, forwarding parameters. Map shape: built-modes handle single split point pipeline, nested pipelines can map arbitrary inputs (e.g. cross-validation folds, several data sets, per-group settings) multiple levels (nested splits). Reuse: nested pipelines inner pipeline standalone, reusable artifact, whereas built-modes steps live single pipeline. Run log state: built-modes produce one unified run partitions, nested pipelines run separately. Parallelism: built-modes handled {pipeflow}, whereas nested pipelines control loop can parallelize .

title: Add a step — pip_add
text: x pipeflow pipeline object. step Unique step name. fun Function execute step. function parameter must default value. Default values simple constants resolved immediately. Default values formulas like ~other_step treated dependencies steps resolved respective output values runtime step executed. tags Optional character vector tags belonging step. Can also adjusted later using [pip_tag()]. Optional position new step inserted (defaults last position). Can step name integer index. set 0, new step inserted beginning pipeline. params Optional named list parameter values, merged defaults fun (overlapping names, default values fun take precedence). two use cases params: Provide param values programmatically adding steps runtime Provide extra param values "mark" dependencies defined pipelines nested step, ensures step (pipeline step) re-executed one respective param values change. exec Execution mode step. One "auto", "split", "reduce" "plain". Using execution mode exec = split, output step marked partitioned output. mode, step depends split step (directly indirectly) output automatically mapped partition-wise step execution. reduce mode expects partitioned input passes without mapping, plain mode accepts non-partitioned input always intends execute single call. summary: auto: map partitioned input appears, otherwise single call split: single call, mark output partitioned reduce: single call, valid partitioned input plain: single call, valid non-partitioned input

title: Replace a step — pip_replace
text: x pipeflow pipeline view object. step Unique step name. fun Function execute step. function parameter must default value. Default values simple constants resolved immediately. Default values formulas like ~other_step treated dependencies steps resolved respective output values runtime step executed. tags Optional character vector tags belonging step. Can also adjusted later using [pip_tag()]. params Optional named list parameter values, merged defaults fun (overlapping names, default values fun take precedence). two use cases params: Provide param values programmatically adding steps runtime Provide extra param values "mark" dependencies defined pipelines nested step, ensures step (pipeline step) re-executed one respective param values change. exec Execution mode step. One "auto", "split", "reduce" "plain". Using execution mode exec = split, output step marked partitioned output. mode, step depends split step (directly indirectly) output automatically mapped partition-wise step execution. reduce mode expects partitioned input passes without mapping, plain mode accepts non-partitioned input always intends execute single call. summary: auto: map partitioned input appears, otherwise single call split: single call, mark output partitioned reduce: single call, valid partitioned input plain: single call, valid non-partitioned input

text: running pipeline can interrupted via restart() halt() virtual methods. intended advanced, self-modifying pipelines often called within step function via .self argument. .self$restart(force = TRUE, times = 1L): aborts current run current step finished restarts first step. default parameters force = TRUE times = 1L, , call just invoking .self$restart(). skip steps already state "done", set force = FALSE. times parameter limits number consecutive restarts within single pip_run() call. view run, restart covers view steps together upstream dependencies. p$halt(): aborts current run current step finished. controlled halt deliberately distinct base::stop(): error raised pipeline marked "failed". run simply ends, steps executed marked "outdated", subsequent pip_run() continue run left . cases steps executed restart halt happens marked "outdated".

code: a <- pip_new("a") |>   pip_add("prep", \(x = 1) x * 2) |>   pip_add("fit", \(x = ~prep) x + 10)  # "prep" exists in both pipelines; the one from b gets a numeric suffix b <- pip_new("b") |> pip_add("prep", \(x = 5) x * 3)  ab <- rbind(a, b) ab[["step"]] # "prep", "fit", "prep2" (step name conflict auto-resolved) #>    prep     fit   prep2  #>  "prep"   "fit" "prep2"  ab #> <pipeflow> a-b (3 steps) #> ------------------------ #>     step params depends state #> 1:  prep      x           new #> 2:   fit      x    prep   new #> 3: prep2      x           new #> ------------------------ #> <ready> last run: never  # Any number of pipelines can be combined abc <- rbind(a, b, b) abc #> <pipeflow> a-b-b (4 steps) #> -------------------------- #>     step params depends state #> 1:  prep      x           new #> 2:   fit      x    prep   new #> 3: prep2      x           new #> 4: prep3      x           new #> -------------------------- #> <ready> last run: never

title: pipeflow 0.3.0
text: C++ DAG engine (src/dag.cpp): graph operations (node/edge add/remove, topological ordering, reachability queries) run C++ speed via Rcpp, eliminating R object overhead dependency resolution. New pip_* API: Functional API replacing R6 Pipeline class — pip_new(), pip_add(), pip_run(), pip_replace(), pip_clone(), pip_bind(), pip_view(), pip_tag()/pip_untag(), etc. Execution modes (auto/split/reduce/plain): Native support map-reduce style workflows steps split output named partitions downstream steps auto-map . Dependency validation definition time: pip_add(), pip_replace(), pip_remove() fail fast broken references. New pkgdown-article pipeflow vs targets (vignettes/articles/v07-vs-targets.Rmd) 18-row feature comparison table benchmarks.

title: pipeflow 0.3.0
text: Legacy pipe_* functions Pipeline R6 class deprecated (preserved aliases R/aliases.R, R/pipelineR6.R). pip_collect_out() longer accepts grouped parameters. returns flat named list step outputs. Use pip_view() tags manual list composition grouped output. group column removed pipeline data.table. Steps previously using group = "..." pip_add() use tags = "...".
